newsitem.title: FRANCE: Japan admitted as Council of Europe observer.
newsitem.headline: Japan admitted as Council of Europe observer.

text.p: The 40-member Council of Europe, set up to promote democracy and human rights, granted Japan observer status on Thursday, saying Tokyo shared the organisation's ideas and values.

"Japan can now name a permanent observer and send observers to committees of government experts and conferences of specialised ministers. It will also be able to join in the activities of certain partial agreements," a council statement said.
The council's committee of ministers considered that "Japan shares the ideas and values" of the organisation, it added.
The United States and Canada were granted observer status at the council early this year. Japan asked to become an observer in July 1995.
